transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Um… I’m here because things at work got a little out of hand, I guess. I work in HR, and I pushed ahead with an onboarding launch before all the approvals were officially in place.

At the time it honestly felt like the right thing — bold, maybe, but necessary. I committed some company money and vendor time, and now… I’m on leave, and people keep asking what I was thinking. I know that probably sounds bad. I’m trying to understand it too.
Can you describe how you were feeling in the days or weeks leading up to that decision at work? Were you feeling more energized, confident, or maybe more irritable than usual?

Yeah… I mean, I’d like to say I was just motivated, but it was probably more than that.

For the past few weeks I felt sort of… brilliantly alive, if that makes sense. Like I could finally show leadership what HR could be if someone just had the courage to move things forward. I felt very confident — maybe too confident.

And then, when people questioned me, even on small things like wording changes or routine budget questions, I’d get suddenly furious. I tried not to show it too much, but inside it felt like they were blocking something important. Does that… does that answer what you mean?
Did you notice this feeling of being 'brilliantly alive' and very confident lasting for several days in a row, or did it come and go more randomly?

It was more… continuous, I think. Not just a good afternoon here and there.

I don’t want to overstate it, but it’s been building for maybe about a month — since the new executive started pushing back on my onboarding redesign. I kept feeling like I had to rise to the moment, if that makes sense. So yes, several days in a row… really more like weeks, though I told myself it was just focus.

Was there a specific time when this feeling of being ‘brilliantly alive’ and very confident was noticeably different from your usual mood, and did it last for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least a week?

Yes… I think there was. I mean, I didn’t think of it as a “mood” at the time — I would’ve called it being focused or finally stepping up.

But looking back, for the past few weeks it was there most days, most of the day. I felt almost… brilliantly alive, like I could finally show leadership what HR could really be. And then if someone questioned me — even small edits or normal budget questions — I’d get suddenly furious inside.

I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but it was definitely different from how I usually am. Does that make sense?

Can you recall if there was a specific period lasting at least a week where your mood was consistently elevated or irritable, different enough that others might have noticed a change in you, even if they didn’t say anything directly?

Yes… I think so. I mean, I wouldn’t have called it elevated at the time, but for the past few weeks there was this stretch where I felt very… alive, almost like I could finally show leadership what HR could be if I just pushed hard enough.

And then the other side of it was that I’d get irritated really fast — not outwardly yelling or anything, but suddenly furious inside when someone questioned me, even about small edits or routine budget questions.

So… yes, I guess it probably was different enough that people might have noticed. I hope that’s the kind of thing you’re asking.

Can you confirm if there was a clear period lasting at least seven days where your mood was noticeably different from usual — such as feeling unusually upbeat, irritable, or 'brilliantly alive' most of the time, even if others didn’t comment on it directly?

Yes… I think I can confirm that. It wasn’t just a day or two.

For the past few weeks, most of the time, I’ve felt either really… brilliantly alive, like I could finally show leadership what HR can be, or I’d swing into feeling suddenly furious when someone questioned me — even about small edits or routine budget things.

I know that probably sounds stronger than I mean it to, but yes, it was noticeably different from my usual.

Can you tell me if there was a specific time when you felt this way — either brilliantly alive or suddenly irritable — for a full week without a break, where it was a consistent part of your day, nearly every day?

Yes… I think so. It’s hard to draw a perfect line around it, but it’s been building for about a month now — since the new executive started challenging my onboarding redesign.

At first I told myself I was just motivated, you know, trying to do good work. But there was definitely at least a week in there where it felt like it was part of almost every day — that energized, “brilliantly alive” feeling, or getting suddenly irritated when I felt pushed back on.

I hope that answers it the way you mean.
